title: event_store/store.zig:337 StoreError.InstanceNotFound on TC-DB-03-01 store.append
notes: Follow-up D2 from the WF03-gh377-20260804 rework-1 retry: after successful tenant provisioning (ISS-0114 fixed), TC-DB-03-01 store.append fails with StoreError.InstanceNotFound at store.zig:337 (line drift since filing; current line ~330). RESOLVED 2026-08-07: root cause corrected during WF03-ISS-0128-20260807 diagnosis. Live instrumentation of src/db/pool.zig and src/event_store/store.zig disproved the originally suspected search_path race -- the connection's search_path was confirmed correct (tenant_default,public) at the moment of the failing lookup. The actual defect is in the TEST ITSELF: TC-DB-03-01 generated a per-run random fixture UUID (inst_id_str) for the instance_projections INSERT, assertions, and cleanup, but called store.append() with a separate, unrelated hardcoded UUID literal ("db0301aa...") that was never inserted anywhere. store.append() was correctly returning InstanceNotFound for a genuinely non-existent instance.
root_cause: CORRECTED: not a race. tests/integration/db_integration_test.zig TC-DB-03-01 called store.append() with a hardcoded UUID literal unrelated to the fixture row's actual id (inst_id_str, a fresh per-run UUID from TestHarness.newUuidString()). The fixture INSERT, post-append assertions, and cleanup all correctly used inst_id_str; only the store.append() call diverged. src/event_store/store.zig and src/db/pool.zig were confirmed defect-free (unchanged; git diff --stat empty on both after diagnosis instrumentation was reverted).
repro_steps: 3. TC-DB-03-01 fails: StoreError.InstanceNotFound (100% reproducible, confirmed on both the shared db_test container and a freshly created + freshly migrated database)
candidate_resolution: SUPERSEDED: the originally proposed resolutions (commit barrier between tenant provisioning and event_store.lookup; explicit schema-qualification in event_store.lookup) were not applied because instrumentation disproved the search_path/race hypothesis they were meant to fix. See resolution field for the fix actually applied.
resolution: Added a local parseUuid(s: []const u8) ![16]u8 helper to tests/integration/db_integration_test.zig (mirrors the existing, established pattern in tests/integration/event_store_integration_test.zig) and changed TC-DB-03-01's store.append() call to derive its instance_id from parseUuid(inst_id_str) -- the SAME fixture UUID used for the INSERT, assertions, and cleanup -- instead of the unrelated hardcoded literal. Verified: zig build exit 0, no error-set output; lint_sql_param_types.py exit 0. TC-DB-03-01 passed 5/5 consecutive zig build test-integration runs post-fix (2 against a fresh DB, 3 against the shared DB) after failing 2/2 (100%) pre-fix on the same two DB types. Regression check via failing-test-name-set diff (pre-fix baseline vs. all 5 post-fix runs): only pre-existing, independently-flaky cross-binary-concurrency tests (TC-DB-01-02, TC-EXP-103-03/04, TC-SCH-303-03 -- ISS-0141/ISS-0148/ISS-0151 class) fluctuated, appearing/disappearing across the 5 post-fix runs themselves with zero code changes between them -- proving pre-existing flakiness, not a regression. TC-DB-03-02's pre-existing exit-code-3 crash is identical before and after and out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: No regression in already-passing event_store tests
prevention: SUPERSEDED (does not apply to the actual root cause found; retained for historical record only): event_store.lookup must qualify its tenant schema explicitly; never rely on the connection's search_path at lookup time.
SUPERSEDED (does not apply): Test flows that combine tenant provisioning + event_store.append must explicitly observe the schema-creation commit before the first append.

ACTUAL PREVENTION: when a test introduces a per-test-random fixture id (e.g. TestHarness.newUuidString()) to fix a hardcoded-identifier isolation bug (the ISS-0113 class), grep the ENTIRE test body for every other identifier used in the same flow before considering the migration complete -- a partial migration that leaves one call site (here, the store.append() instance_id argument) on the old hardcoded literal reads as fully isolated until that specific call site is exercised, and the resulting failure (InstanceNotFound) is easy to misattribute to the production code under test rather than the test's own fixture wiring.

Before accepting a filed issue's stated root-cause hypothesis (especially one drawing an analogy to a recently-fixed sibling issue, as this one did to ISS-0130), reproduce the failure and instrument the actual code path rather than assuming the analogy holds -- direct instrumentation here took under 30 minutes and definitively ruled out the search_path/race hypothesis that had been carried in the issue record for 3 days.
